scope: Proposition 9.1 of the manuscript “Metric descent and rank-preserving contractions” (preprints/Metric-descent-and-rank-preserving-contractions-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 068 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 35f14f53ac82dc8a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 49. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X, Y be smooth connected projective varieties, let L = −KX have a smooth semipositive metric, and let an algebraic torus T act on X. Suppose that f : X 99K Y is dominant and invariant and that every invariant rational function on X having no poles at the f-horizontal prime divisors of X belongs to C(Y ). Choose a normal projective graph model X p ← − W φ − → Y on which every vertical prime maps onto a prime divisor of Y . Let N be the reduced sum of the primes of Y above which all prime divisors of W are exceptional over X. For every dominant rational map g : Y 99K U to a smooth projective variety, let F ⊂ TY be the saturated sheaf tangent to its general fibers. There is an integer c ≥ 0 such that det(TY /F) + cN is pseudoeffective. Consequently, if α ̸= 0 is a movable curve class on Y with α · N = 0, then every line subsheaf A ⊂ (Ω1 Y )⊗j, j ≥ 0, satisfies α · c1(A) ≤ 0.
